children: posted an 8% rise in first-quarter cash profit on Wednesday, helped by higher lending and deposit volumes, but the number of home loan applications slid 16% as high interest rates and new tax reforms dented demand.
Australia's top bank reported a cash net profit after tax of A$2.8 billion ($1.92 billion) for the three months ended September 30, up from last year's A$2.6 billion.
Business lending volumes rose 13.6% during the quarter, while household deposits climbed nearly 8%
Australia lifted its policy rate to an 18-year high of 4.85% last week, citing inflationary pressures
Tax reforms introduced earlier this year have also dented mortgage demand, one of the bank's biggest revenue drivers
But home lending volumes still grew 6.6%
"Higher inflation and interest rates continue to place uneven pressure on household incomes and business activity," said CEO Matt Comyn
CBA said home loan arrears increased by 7 basis points during the quarter
The bank's net interest margin, the difference between lending and deposit rates, was broadly stable
CBA's common equity tier 1 (level 2) ratio, a measure of spare cash, increased 36 basis points to 11.5% as of September end
CBA brought the curtain down on the bank earnings season, which carried warnings of a prolonged housing downturn and mounting recession risks
